correctness.rationale: A direct Chevalley–Eilenberg two-term differential gives Betti numbers as consecutive nullities of additive exterior derivations. Over the finite-field splitting extension, their eigenvalues are sums of distinct Frobenius conjugates, so nullities count codewords of each weight. The normal-basis Frobenius module identifies every cyclic code ideal (g) with the annihilator of (X^d−1)/g; absence of weights one and two proves full degree. Both steps cover all d>=2, including inseparable factorization of X^d−1. Direct finite-field exterior-matrix and code checks agree for 21 irreducible polynomials degrees 2–6, with all 11 eligible cyclic-code realizations independently verified; finite checks are corroborative only. The two primitive F_8 examples differ in characteristic polynomials.

value.rationale: The theorem classifies all attainable trivial-coefficient Betti polynomials of an infinite irreducible almost-abelian Lie family by independently motivated cyclic-code Hamming spectra and proves every eligible code is realized, not merely a single computed invariant. It structurally detects normal bases by cohomological vanishing, proves H²=0 throughout, and separates nonisomorphic primitive-element examples. This is a natural complete classification with reusable implications in modular Lie theory and field arithmetic, not just a finite census.
